messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: p99 streaming latency spike detected for /v1/generate (region: us-west-2). SLA breach threshold crossed at 15:23 UTC. Autoscaler added capacity but tail latency remains high. Logs: error rate ~0.3%, p95 ~420ms, p99 ~3.8s.

oncall-maya: on it. are we seeing any model fallbacks? what hosts?

sre-jen: initial look — correlates with GPU node degradation on cluster-gpu-7. NVML reports correctable ECC errors and repeated thermal throttling events since 15:18. Streaming requests to that node show long kv-cache stall times.

infra-ryan: pulling node logs now. `ssh gpu-node-7` shows repeated ECC correctable counts incrementing, temperature ramp to 92C, fan oscillation. Might be flaky card or PCI thermal sensor.

ops-jordan: customers impacted: 3 high-traffic tenants (prod apps). CS-alyssa is contacting top 2. Started routing-to-fallback-models as temporary mitigation (lower-capacity quantized replicas).

cs-alyssa: pinging customer contacts, telling them we see elevated tail latency and we're mitigating. ETA for updates: 15 min.

incident-bot: action required: oncall -> perform live mitigation. Suggested playbook: 1) cordon/evacuate affected node 2) route traffic off node 3) trigger model fallback to compatible replicas 4) escalate HW if node doesn't recover.

oncall-maya: starting evacuation. `kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then move traffic.

deploy-bot: Rolling update triggered for route /v1/generate with fallback policy v2-quantized (traffic weight 40%) -> applied.

sre-jen: Observed immediate reduction in p95 to ~260ms after routing 35% traffic to quantized fallback. p99 still elevated from inflight streams stuck on kv cache. Investigating streaming runtime stack traces.

infra-ryan: ran `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,fan.speed,ecc.correctable.errors --format=csv` output:

```
# gpu-id, temperature.gpu, fan.speed, ecc.correctable.errors
0, 92, 12 %, 342
1, 45, 42 %, 2
2, 46, 40 %, 0
```

-- gpu 0 is the noisy offender. Fan controller responded but oscillated. Looks hardware-level.

ops-jordan: starting node quarantine. marking `gpu-node-7` for HW maintenance. spinning up replacement nodes to keep capacity.

oncall-maya: handoff note: I'll stay on for next 30m while infra validates replacements. If p99 drops below 800ms and customers confirm, we'll close incident. Otherwise escalate to hardware vendor.

cs-alyssa: customer A acknowledged impact and accepted fallback. Customer B asked for more details; shared the incident page and that we are evacuating GPU node.

sre-jen: follow-up check: streaming stalls appear tied to KV cache eviction thrash when requests hit the degraded GPU — some long-running inference sessions didn't gracefully reattach to new cache leading to tail stalls. Implemented short-term: reduce per-session streaming buffer timeout from 120s -> 30s to limit stuck streams.

infra-ryan: replacement nodes up (3x gpus) and router drained traffic from gpu-node-7. Observability shows p99 trending down: 3.8s -> 1.1s -> 680ms over 12 minutes.

oncall-maya: good. updating incident channel and PagerDuty. leaving detailed remediation steps for postmortem: run hardware full diagnostics, add node-level thermal alarms earlier (temp > 85C), adjust autoscaler to prefer draining on ECC correctable spikes.

ops-jordan: created ticket HW-4872 assigned to infra-ryan for vendor support / RMA. Also PR to runtime: `streaming: reduce-default-buffer-timeout` in review.

cs-alyssa: customers updated: both opened support threads; CS will follow up with status email and mitigation details.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. SLA: partial breach for 00:06:42. Owner: oncall-maya. Postmortem owner: sre-jen.

sre-jen: postmortem notes I'll collect: timeline, root cause (GPU thermal/fan oscillation + ECC correctable accumulation leading to runtime KV stalls), mitigation and follow-ups (hardware RMA, thermal alarm thresholds, fallback routing improvements, session timeout change).

oncall-maya: closing handoff. leaving a sticky with runbook updates. will hand back to normal oncall at 16:05 UTC.

ops-jordan: thumbs up. will ensure HW ticket gets vendor priority. :white_check_mark:

cs-alyssa: final customer summary drafted, will send once postmortem has first draft.

incident-bot: thread archived when postmortem link posted. keep updates here only for the record.
